[Thinking]
**Summarizing Progress M-14M Mission**

I need to summarize the Russian cargo mission Progress M-14M to the ISS. It launched on January 26, 2012, using a Soyuz-U rocket from Baikonur, docking on January 28, and undocking on April 19. The spacecraft delivered around 2.6 tons of supplies, including fuel and food. It was the first to utilize the upgraded digital flight control system "TsVM-101" and also tested the new "Kurs-NA" rendezvous system. There was a communication issue to note as well.
[/Thinking]

Progress M-14M (Russian: Прогресс М-14М) was an uncrewed Russian **Progress** cargo spacecraft mission to the **International Space Station (ISS)** operated by **Roscosmos/RSC Energia**. It was part of the long-running Progress resupply program and used the “Progress-M” variant.

## Identity / vehicle
- **Spacecraft type:** Progress-M (uncrewed cargo ship derived from Soyuz)
- **Common alternate designation:** sometimes listed as **Progress 46P** (the 46th Progress mission to dock with the ISS)
- **Launched by:** **Soyuz-U** rocket
- **Launch site:** **Baikonur Cosmodrome**, Kazakhstan

## Mission purpose
Progress M-14M’s role was the standard set of Progress duties:
- Deliver **food, water, oxygen/air supplies, clothing, spares, and scientific equipment**
- Deliver **propellant** (for ISS propulsion needs and/or station reboost operations, depending on mission planning)
- Provide a vehicle for **trash disposal** (it is loaded with waste before departure and burns up during reentry)

## Timeline (key events)
- **Launch:** **26 January 2012**
- **Docking:** **28 January 2012**  
  - Docked to the **Pirs Docking Compartment (DC-1)** on the Russian segment of the ISS
- **Undocking / departure:** **19 April 2012**
- **End of mission:** After departure it performed a controlled deorbit and **burned up in Earth’s atmosphere** over the remote South Pacific (the usual disposal profile for Progress vehicles)

## Cargo (high level)
Like other Progress flights of that era, M-14M carried **on the order of a few tons** of mixed cargo, typically including:
- **Dry cargo:** food, hygiene items, crew provisions, spare parts/tools
- **Life-support consumables:** water and gases (e.g., oxygen/air components)
- **Propellant:** transferred through the docking interface to Russian-segment tanks as required
- **Items for experiments and station maintenance**

(Exact kilogram-by-kilogram manifests exist in mission documentation and press releases, but at a high level it was a “routine” multi-category ISS logistics load.)

## Operations while attached to ISS
While berthed to Pirs, Progress M-14M could be used for:
- **Cargo transfer** to the station and later **waste loading**
- Periodic use of its systems as part of **ISS propulsion planning** (Progress vehicles can support reboost planning; actual burns depend on schedule and which docked craft is tasked)
- Supporting routine Russian-segment logistics during **Expedition 30/31** timeframe (early 2012)

## End-of-life / disposal
Progress spacecraft do not return to Earth. After undocking, M-14M:
- Conducted a **deorbit burn**
- Entered the atmosphere and **disintegrated**, with any surviving fragments falling into the designated remote oceanic disposal region

## Context / significance
Progress M-14M is best described as a **standard, successful ISS resupply mission** in 2012:
- Used the well-established **Soyuz-U + Progress-M** combination
- Docked to **Pirs**, delivered supplies, and later removed waste
- Completed a normal destructive reentry disposal after several weeks attached to the ISS

If you want, tell me whether you’re looking for a **full technical profile** (dimensions, mass breakdown, propulsion system, Kurs rendezvous suite, etc.) or a **day-by-day mission log**, and I’ll expand in that direction.
